programmes.programme: Sure Start NI (38 projects; DE-funded, SPPG-administered)

outcomes.measure: Children whose Hanen Communication & Language stage progressed by at least one stage from Autumn 24 to Spring 25 or who remained at the highest stage on this measure
outcomes.comparison: none (single-group change over the year; no comparison group); baseline is the child's own Autumn 2024 stage
outcomes.cohort: Children in the Developmental Programme for 2-3 Year Olds, excluding bilingual children
outcomes.note: Complement: 191 (15%) 'stayed at the same Hanen Communication & Language stage'. The measure counts 'remained at the highest stage' as success.

outcomes.measure: Children whose language and communication development progressed by at least one stage from Autumn 24 to Spring 25 or who remained at the highest stage on this measure (as monitored by BLP)
outcomes.comparison: none (single-group change over the year; no comparison group)
outcomes.cohort: Bilingual children in the Developmental Programme for 2-3 Year Olds (Sure Start Bilingual Language Profile)
outcomes.note: 10 (5%) stayed at the same stage.

outcomes.measure: Number of children screened - who showed improvement (WellComm)
outcomes.comparison: pre/post WellComm screen; no comparison group
outcomes.cohort: Children attending DP2-3YO screened pre and post, academic year 2024/2025
outcomes.note: 'Improvement defined as progressed towards Green or Stayed Green'. 431 (32%) did not show improvement; 'All 431 children received additional support'. 144 eligible (10%) were not screened pre and post (absent on one or both dates).

outcomes.measure: Outcomes Star: In 1+ outcome areas - Percentage of people making progress in at least one outcome area
outcomes.comparison: first vs second Star reading; no comparison group
outcomes.cohort: Sure Start service users who completed first and second star readings after a Sure Start intervention
outcomes.note: Out of 1,675 who completed at least 1 Star reading. Also: 2+ areas 76%; 3+ areas 58%; average number of outcome areas showing progress 3.2.

outcomes.measure: Outcomes Star 'Made progress' by outcome area
outcomes.value: Physical health 41%; Emotional well-being 57%; Keeping your children safe 25%; Social networks 50%; Boundaries & routines 48%; Child development 49%; Home, money and work 45%
outcomes.note: Other categories per area are 'Maintained at end point', 'Maintained (not at end point)' and 'Dropped back' (6-7% dropped back in each area). Read from the labelled chart image.

outcomes.measure: Percentage of children registered before 1st birthday
outcomes.comparison: endnote says it increased year on year
outcomes.note: Reach/process measure, not an outcome. 70% of eligible children 0-3 were registered at 31 March 2025.

outcomes.measure: % of Children Overweight or Obese (IOTF), BMI levels in Primary 1
outcomes.value: Living in Sure Start areas 23.5%; not living in Sure Start areas 19.8%; all children 21.3%
outcomes.cohort: All P1 children by area of residence (NIMDM 2017 Sure Start areas)
outcomes.note: AREA-LEVEL contextual indicator: compares residents of Sure Start areas with other residents, not Sure Start users with non-users. Cannot be attributed to the programme.

outcomes.measure: % of Mothers who Smoked During Pregnancy (recorded at antenatal booking appointment)
outcomes.value: Sure Start areas 14.80%; not Sure Start areas 5.70%; all 9.70%
outcomes.note: Area-level. Excludes women delivering in SEHSCT between 9/11/23 and 31/3/24 (EPIC data).

outcomes.measure: % of Children Breastfeeding at Hospital Discharge
outcomes.value: Sure Start areas 43.6%; not Sure Start areas 57.7%; all 51.8%
outcomes.comparison: area comparison; later time points to 12 months also given (13.3% / 20.4% / 17.5% at 12 months)
outcomes.cohort: Live infants born to NI residents
outcomes.note: Area-level contextual indicator.

outcomes.measure: % of Year 1-7 primary pupils with a statement of SEN
outcomes.value: Sure Start areas 7.90%; not Sure Start areas 5.70%
outcomes.note: Area-level. Same page: % of leavers with 5 GCSEs A*-C including English and Maths, 2023/24: 63.80% Sure Start areas vs 76.50% other areas; 2024/25 no data.

outcomes.measure: ETI: language and communication progress
outcomes.value: 'almost all of the children are making very good progress in their language and communication skills'
outcomes.unit: ETI quantitative term ('almost/nearly all' = more than 90%)
outcomes.comparison: 'Comparison with baseline assessments following speech and language intervention' (the projects' WellComm data)
outcomes.cohort: Children in DP2-3YO at 5 of 38 projects (16 settings)
outcomes.measureType: inspector judgement drawing on practitioner baseline assessments
outcomes.page: Summary; section 'the staff are successful in improving the children's language skills'
outcomes.note: Not a percentage. ETI's quantitative-terms key is in Appendix 4.

outcomes.measure: ETI: overall developmental progress
outcomes.value: 'almost all of the children are making very good progress from their individual starting points'
outcomes.note: The same report finds the transition to pre-school 'is not as effective as it could be'.

outcomes.measure: Parental survey: rating of Sure Start project
outcomes.value: 90% of respondents rating their Sure Start project as 'excellent'
outcomes.cohort: SPPG parental survey across the 38 Sure Start projects, June 2023
outcomes.note: Satisfaction, not an outcome. The survey itself was not found published; it is cited only inside the ETI report.

evaluations.title: An evaluation of Sure Start's Developmental Programme for 2 to 3-year-old children and the effectiveness of its play-based activities in achieving positive outcomes for the children's development
evaluations.author: Education and Training Inspectorate (ETI)
evaluations.design: qualitative (inspection: observation of 149 children in 16 settings at 5 projects; discussions with 96 parents, staff and SPPG; documentation review)
evaluations.summary: ETI's fifth Sure Start evaluation since 2018. Judges that almost all children make very good progress, citing language assessments before and after intervention; no percentages and no comparison group. Archived copy: https://dera.ioe.ac.uk/id/eprint/42024/1/an-evaluation-of-sure-starts-developmental-programme-for-2-to-3-year-old-children-and-the-effectiveness-of-its.pdf

evaluations.title: Sure Start Annual Report Card 2024/2025 (OBA)
evaluations.author: Department of Education / SPPG
evaluations.design: pre-post monitoring (no comparison group) plus area-level administrative indicators
evaluations.summary: Language: Hanen 85%, BLP 95%, WellComm 68% improved. Parenting: Outcomes Star 94% progress in 1+ area (n=627). The 'Is anyone better off?' section is area-level population data (Sure Start areas vs others), not outcomes for users.

evaluations.title: Parental perspectives of involvement in a Sure Start programme in Northern Ireland: impact on wellbeing
evaluations.author: Elaine K. Duddy (European Early Childhood Education Research Journal 30(6):867-882)
evaluations.design: qualitative (constructivist grounded theory; interviews with mothers at one rural project)
evaluations.summary: Reports benefits to maternal wellbeing and mental health; no quantified outcomes.

evaluations.title: Evaluating the impact of Sure Start (Northern Ireland) using a naturally occurring experiment and a longitudinal birth cohort (project E102)
evaluations.author: Cardiff University (M. L. Zhang), via HDR Gateway / NI TRE
evaluations.design: quasi-experimental (natural experiment on expansion waves, linked administrative data) - IN PROGRESS
evaluations.summary: Data-access approval dated 10/01/2025; no published results found.

programmes.gaps: No published comparison-group or counterfactual outcome evaluation of NI Sure Start since 2019; the E102 linked-data study is in progress and has no outputs found. The OBA card's 'better off' indicators are area-level (residents of Sure Start areas vs others), not participants vs non-participants, and cannot be attributed to the programme. School readiness: no measure found (the GCSE and SEN rows are area-level; ETI judges readiness qualitatively). The 2023 SPPG parental survey is cited by ETI but was not found published.

outcomes.measure: Families Referred that were Linked to a Service or Other Reasons for Outcome of Referral: Achieved - linked to 1 service
outcomes.cohort: Families referred through Family Support Hubs, 2024/25
outcomes.note: Text: '52% of families referred to the Hubs were signposted to a single service'. This is a linkage/output measure, not a change in family circumstances. The remaining slices (4%, 3%, 3%, 2%, 2%, 2%) carry the labels Did not engage, Open to Social Services, No consent, Above threshold and No available service, but the chart does not map each value to a label unambiguously.

outcomes.measure: Achieved - linked to more than 1 service
outcomes.note: '65% of families in Northern Hubs and just 1 family in South Eastern being connected to more than one service.'

outcomes.measure: Referral Process: Achieved in 4 weeks
outcomes.note: Achieved in 5-8 weeks: 232, 106, 223, 188. '244 were processed but exceeded the eight-week timescale, while 145 were not achieved within the regional timescale.' Timeliness, not an outcome.

outcomes.measure: Number of Parents/Children referred who did and did not take up the service offer
outcomes.value: by Trust area (chart)
outcomes.note: Uptake/output. The mapping of chart labels to values is partly ambiguous in the extracted text, so no values are recorded.

outcomes.measure: Unmet need: Parenting programmes/parenting support
outcomes.value: 157 (9 hubs)
outcomes.comparison: also the top unmet need in 2023/24
outcomes.note: The report says recording of unmet need is still being standardised.

evaluations.title: Family Support Hubs Annual Report Card 2024/25

evaluations.summary: Produced December 2025. 'How much' and 'How well' measures only; there is NO 'Is anyone better off?' section.

evaluations.title: Family Support Hubs in Northern Ireland (SCIE review)
evaluations.author: SCIE
evaluations.summary: Pre-2019; not examined for figures here.

programmes.gaps: The 2024/25 report card has no outcome measure: no % of families whose needs were met, no distance travelled, and no measure of escalation to social services avoided. 'Open to Social Services' appears only as a reason a referral was not achieved. No post-2019 outcome evaluation of the Hubs was found. The CYPSP Hubs overview brief (strongertogetherni.org, 2025) contains no outcome figures.

evaluations.title: Adult and Youth Reoffending in Northern Ireland (2022/23 Cohort)
evaluations.author: DoJ Analytical Services Group / NISRA
evaluations.design: administrative cohort statistics (no matching or adjustment)
evaluations.summary: Tables: https://www.justice-ni.gov.uk/system/files/2025-10/Adult%20and%20Youth%20Reoffending%20in%20Northern%20Ireland%20%2820223%20Cohort%29%20-%20Tables.ods . 2021/22 cohort tables: https://www.justice-ni.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/justice/Adult%20and%20Youth%20Reoffending%20in%20Northern%20Ireland%20%28202122%20Cohort%29%20-%20Tables.ods . The next release (2023/24 cohort) is confirmed for 4 November 2026.

evaluations.title: Youth Justice Agency Annual Report and Accounts 2025-26
evaluations.author: Youth Justice Agency
evaluations.summary: Its outcome measures are process/participation measures (victim participation, report timeliness, reintegration plans); it gives no reoffending or wellbeing outcome for conference participants. It notes a QUB evaluation of the YJA/CAMHS partnership, with a phase 2 effectiveness study from 2026-27.

programmes.gaps: No published adjusted or matched comparison of youth conferences against other disposals; DoJ explicitly warns against comparing raw rates by disposal. The 2023/24 cohort is not yet published (due 4 Nov 2026). The YJA Annual Workload Statistics 2025-26 (ODS) contain counts only, no outcomes. No published victim-satisfaction figure for youth conferences was found for 2019 onward.

programmes.programme: VOYPIC (Voice of Young People in Care) - Independent Advocacy and Participation

outcomes.measure: 92% said they had influenced decision making ('Is anyone better off?')
outcomes.cohort: Young people who completed an evaluation of the Independent Advocacy Service

outcomes.measure: 77% said their rights were protected
96% felt listened to ('How well did we do?')
98% would use the VOYPIC Advocacy Service again
reported their case was fully resolved
outcomes.value: '873.2% (349)' as printed
outcomes.note: The printed percentage is a typo. The printed count (349) is larger than the stated 335 cases completed, and the headline '335 advocacy support cases were completed' is identical to 2023-24, so treat these figures as unreliable. As printed: partially resolved 13.6% (65); unresolved 0.4% (2); withdrawn 2.3% (11); circumstance changed 10.5% (50).

outcomes.measure: Young People's Skills Development (participation programmes)
outcomes.value: Speaking Up 62%; Building Better Relationships 60%; Listening 51%; Decision Making 41%; Leadership 36%

outcomes.measure: children and young people said they have a better quality of life
outcomes.note: Also: more independence 74 (46%); more personal dignity & respect 56 (35%); more access to community services 34 (24%); 65% said they know more about their rights. These items do not appear in the 2024-25 report.

evaluations.title: VOYPIC Annual Report 2024-2025
evaluations.author: VOYPIC
evaluations.design: service self-evaluation (questionnaire after the service only)
evaluations.summary: 715 advocacy issues resolved; 444 children and young people received SPPG-funded advocacy; 181 evaluations returned.

evaluations.title: VOYPIC Annual Report 2023-2024
evaluations.author: VOYPIC
evaluations.summary: 161 evaluations; includes quality-of-life and independence items.

programmes.gaps: No independent evaluation of VOYPIC advocacy was found for 2019 onward. Every outcome figure is self-report collected only after the service, from a subset of service users (181 of 444), with no baseline or comparison. The 2024-25 case-resolution figures are internally inconsistent.

outcomes.measure: Parentline NI supported 7,070 parents and carers, and is exceeding annual targets.
outcomes.note: Output only. The same page says 'Feedback continued to highlight the service's life-changing impact' but gives no figure.

programmes.gaps: No outcome measure was found for Parentline NI. The CiNI trustees' report 2024-25 gives reach only, the CiNI Parentline webpage gives no figures, and no evaluation was found. Evaluations of 'Parentline Plus' (England) exist but must not be applied to NI.

programmes.programme: Early Intervention Support Service (EISS, PHA; five HSC Trust services)

outcomes.measure: Main effects: TOPSE_Empathy, adjusted post-test mean, intervention vs control
outcomes.comparison: non-randomised wait-list control, adjusted for pre-test score
outcomes.cohort: Parents completing pre- and post-test measures across four EISS (no Belfast Trust data)
outcomes.note: Only 2 of 22 outcomes were significant (TOPSE Empathy; TOPSE Play g .56, p=.039). The authors write that 'the current evaluation has not found any robust evidence that the intervention has been effective', and that both results may 'reflect random fluctuations'. The printed confidence interval for Empathy crosses zero despite p=.014 (as printed).

outcomes.measure: Main effects: SDQ_Difficulties
outcomes.note: Not significant. Also not significant: PSI_Total_Stress 116.2 vs 121.4, g -.27, p=.241; FFS Score g .09, p=.724.

outcomes.measure: Family Star Plus: % of cases whose score Increased, by domain (cases with an initial score of 9 or less)
outcomes.value: Meeting emotional needs 78.5%; Boundaries and behaviour 81.0%; Your well-being 71.4%; Family routine 68.9%; Physical health 41.5%; Progress to work 38.4%
outcomes.comparison: initial vs final Star; no control
outcomes.note: The authors note these are parents' perceptions, 'susceptible to bias', and that without a control group the change cannot be attributed. Rows were matched to domains by the order of the extracted table and checked against the report's text.

evaluations.title: An Evaluation of the Early Intervention Support Service in Northern Ireland
evaluations.author: Winter, K., Neeson, L., Sweet, D. and Connolly, P. (QUB Centre for Evidence and Social Innovation)
evaluations.design: comparison group (non-randomised wait-list control) + qualitative process evaluation (55 interviews) + Outcomes Star psychometric analysis
evaluations.summary: No robust evidence of effect; small sample; 2 of 22 outcomes significant. The process evaluation was positive. Mirror: https://pure.qub.ac.uk/portal/files/155982564/FINAL_EISS_Report_110618.pdf

evaluations.title: The UNCRC and Family Support: A Case Study of the Early Intervention Support Service
evaluations.author: Child Care in Practice (Taylor & Francis)
evaluations.summary: Not opened; listed as the post-2019 EISS literature located.

evaluations.title: Evaluation of the alcohol/drug enhancement of the EISS
evaluations.author: PHA Health Intelligence
evaluations.summary: Listed in the PHA Annual Report 2024/25 as work undertaken ('The evaluation is due early 2025'); not found published.

programmes.gaps: The only outcome evaluation predates 2019 (2018) and found no robust effect. The PHA Annual Report 2024/25 says EISS works with 800+ families per year but publishes no outcomes. The 2025 evaluation of the substance-use enhancement was not found online.

outcomes.measure: Q. Did you feel it was beneficial in any of the below areas? [parents, Family Group]

outcomes.value: Improved Social Skills 81%; Improved Communication Skills 76%; Enjoyment with Parent 81%; Learning Opportunities 95%; Increased Confidence 76%; Increased Independence 81%
outcomes.cohort: As above (parents reporting about their child)

outcomes.measure: say they're more able to cope with feeling isolated

evaluations.title: Home-Start Northern Ireland Impact Report 2019
evaluations.author: Home-Start UK
evaluations.design: pre-post monitoring (Journey of Change scale; no comparison)
evaluations.summary: The latest NI-wide Home-Start impact figures found. Landing page: https://www.home-start.org.uk/our-impact-in-northern-ireland

evaluations.title: Home-Start North Down trustees' annual report, y/e 31 March 2024
evaluations.author: Home-Start North Down
evaluations.summary: One scheme; respondent count not stated. Its y/e 31 March 2025 report filed with CCNI is a single page with no extractable text.

programmes.gaps: No NI-wide Home-Start outcome figures were found after the 2019 Impact Report (2018 data). Scheme-level figures exist only where a scheme publishes them (North Down 2023/24 checked; the other 15 schemes were not checked). No independent NI evaluation was found. UK-wide Home-Start outcome percentages exist but must not be applied to NI.

programmes.programme: Family Nurse Partnership NI (PHA; one team per HSC Trust)

outcomes.measure: The annual cost per case/client of services avoided as a result of FNP
outcomes.value: in the range of approximately £40,000 - £485,000
outcomes.cohort: Based on 10 of the 23 deepened client stories (from 69 analysable of 80+ collected)
outcomes.page: PDF p.81 (printed p.77) 'Summary of the Financial Paper'
outcomes.note: Bands (printed p.78): High £485k, Medium £122K, Low £39k. The report claims a return 'at least 6:1 rising to 97:1' at individual client level for short-run savings: an evaluator claim for individual cases, not the whole programme. 'Around 30-45 currently live cases are likely to be avoiding annualized costs each of £122,000 - £485,000'.

outcomes.measure: FNP at least saves other services more than its current annual cost
outcomes.value: qualitative claim
outcomes.note: A statement by the revaluation team; no programme-level figure.

outcomes.measure: Attrition: of the 653 clients ever enrolled by 31/12/2016, 8 (1.4%) left during pregnancy, 29 (7.3%) left during infancy and 22 (6.6%) left during toddlerhood
outcomes.value: as stated
outcomes.cohort: All FNP NI clients enrolled to 31/12/2016
outcomes.note: Retention, not an outcome. Pre-2019.

evaluations.title: Family Nurse Partnership Transforming Lives in Northern Ireland: Public Health Agency response to the revaluation of Family Nurse Partnership in Northern Ireland
evaluations.author: Deirdre Webb, PHA (revaluation by Learning Studio Ltd with AD Research & Analysis and the Strategic Investment Board NI)
evaluations.design: qualitative (revaluation: participative storytelling, 80+ stories) with cost-avoidance estimates for individual cases
evaluations.summary: Client stories illustrate improvements over the life course (child development, maternal mental health, self-efficacy); no quantified child or parent outcome rates. Includes vulnerability profiling of the caseload (n=308).

evaluations.title: Adaptation and implementation of an intervention to identify and respond to intimate partner violence in the family nurse partnership Northern Ireland program
evaluations.author: Child Abuse & Neglect
evaluations.summary: Covers implementation and acceptability, not client outcomes.

programmes.gaps: No NI FNP outcome data (breastfeeding, smoking, immunisation, child development) was found published for 2019 onward. The PHA Annual Report 2024/25 lists an FNP International Annual Report 2024 and five HSCT Annual Review Reports 2024; none was found online. The only NI evaluation is the 2017-18 revaluation (qualitative, pre-2019). The England Building Blocks RCT and the Scotland evaluation must not be applied to NI.

meta.rules: measures quoted verbatim; nothing computed; area-level and single-scheme figures flagged; nothing generalised across places or jurisdictions
